A score is a claim about the future: roughly how well a model will predict data it has not
seen. This section asks what such a score can claim and what it should measure, on the
same simulated survey as the rest of the course.
The first two pages cover the folds:

- **cross-validation**: five or ten folds of sites are enough, their out-of-fold
  predictions are pooled into one score, and nested cross-validation scores a search for
  the best model as well as the model it picks;
- **spatial and temporal cross-validation**: a score says how well a model predicts
  stations as far from its fitted data as the held-out ones were, so blocks as wide as the
  patches in its errors test new areas, and a forecast is tested on later years.

The next two cover the measures:

- **regression performance measures**: RMSE, MAE, the Poisson deviance and R² weigh misses
  their own way and can choose different models, and the squared correlation often
  reported as R² cannot see predictions that run low;
- **classification performance measures**: presence can be scored on the calls at one
  threshold, on how well the probabilities rank the stations, or on the probabilities
  themselves.

The last two cover what to report:

- **uncertainty and stability**: a bootstrap of the sites puts an interval on a score, and
  a paired comparison says how sure a ranking of two models is;
- **choosing measures that match the objective**: the use of the predictions decides the
  measure, a shortlist is scored on the animals it finds, and the costs of misses and
  false alarms set the threshold.

The section picks up threads from earlier ones.
[Hyperparameter selection](../05-generalisation/hyperparameter-selection.qmd) chose a
setting by cross-validation by site; [Cross-validation](cross-validation.qmd) shows that
the folds that choose a model cannot also score it.
[Spatial and temporal dependence](../06-assumptions-limitations/spatial-and-temporal-dependence.qmd)
compared folds of sites with spatial blocks, and
[Spatial and temporal cross-validation](spatial-and-temporal-cv.qmd) sets the width of the
blocks from the model's errors.
[Distributional assumptions](../06-assumptions-limitations/distributional-assumptions.qmd)
showed that each loss aims at a different middle of the data;
[Regression performance measures](regression-metrics.qmd) shows what that does to the
scores. [Class imbalance](../06-assumptions-limitations/class-imbalance.qmd) counted
misses and false alarms apart at one threshold;
[Classification performance measures](classification-metrics.qmd) scores the ranking and
the probabilities, and [Choosing measures that match the objective](choosing-a-metric.qmd)
chooses the threshold from the costs.
[Independence of observations](../06-assumptions-limitations/independence-of-observations.qmd)
resampled whole sites to measure what repeat visits are worth;
[Uncertainty and stability](uncertainty-and-stability.qmd) resamples them to put an
interval on a score.

## Further resources

**Documentation**

- [Evaluate your model with resampling](https://www.tidymodels.org/start/resampling/), tidymodels.
- [rsample](https://rsample.tidymodels.org/) and [yardstick](https://yardstick.tidymodels.org/), tidymodels. Every resampling scheme, and every metric with its definition.
- [Cross-validation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/cross_validation.html) and [metrics and scoring](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html), scikit-learn user guide. Its section on grouped data covers cross-validation by site.
